items.title: SPHMC M-kappa phase metric and moment adapter

source.anchor: M-kappa display before Theorem 4.5; Lemma D.4 proof
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS supplies explicit comparison constants and the omitted near-optimal-coupling details.

items.statement: The paper's exact twisted phase transport cost controls ordinary phase transport and therefore transfers reference position/momentum moments to an incoming law.
assumptions: Explicit reference second moments for the final adapter.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper gives a positive matrix for kappa>=1.
assumption_deltas.lean: The definition is total; positivity is proved only under kappa>=1 in the consumer module proof.
assumption_deltas.reason: Separating a total definition from its valid parameter domain avoids hidden partiality.

bindings.boundary: Raw squared transport infimum; no optimizer.

assumption_deltas.lean: ASTIS stores its square directly as an ENNReal Kantorovich value.
assumption_deltas.reason: The paper consumers use the squared quantity; ENNReal preserves infinite costs.

bindings.boundary: One-way explicit comparison only; no D.3.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper says the norms are uniformly equivalent.
assumption_deltas.lean: ASTIS proves the explicit kappa-uniform one-way constant 6 needed by Lemma D.4.
assumption_deltas.reason: The constant follows from the displayed matrix by Cauchy--Schwarz and a completed square.

assumption_deltas.source: Finite-dimensional Euclidean optimal couplings are available.
assumption_deltas.lean: The proof uses near-optimal couplings and arbitrary measures.
assumption_deltas.reason: Attainment is unnecessary for the inequality.

bindings.boundary: Metric/moment adapter only; D.3, history, D.7, D.8 and main theorems remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: The stationary phase law and Lemma 4.16 supply moments in the paper.
assumption_deltas.lean: Reference integrability and bounds Mx,Mp are explicit premises.
assumption_deltas.reason: This theorem isolates the metric step from stationary-law construction.
